title: Maximum Distance in Arrays
summary: Given m sorted arrays, select one element from each array to maximize the absolute difference between the chosen elements.
statement: Given m sorted arrays, select one element from each array to maximize the absolute difference between the chosen elements.
constraints: 2 <= len(arrays) <= 100,000; every inner array is nonempty and sorted.
Choose values from two different arrays and maximize their absolute difference.
reference_solution:
def maximum_array_distance(arrays):
    smallest, largest = arrays[0][0], arrays[0][-1]
    answer = 0
    for row in arrays[1:]:
        answer = max(answer, abs(row[-1] - smallest), abs(largest - row[0]))
        smallest = min(smallest, row[0])
        largest = max(largest, row[-1])
    return answer

hints: Only each sorted array’s endpoints can maximize distance.
Before incorporating a new array, compare its endpoints with extrema from earlier arrays.
Track global smallest/largest; test new max-old min and old max-new min.
Comparing before updating guarantees the two selected values come from different arrays.
